title: We Tested 9 Free AI Website Builders: The Best One in 2026
summary: We tested the free tier of nine AI website builders, not just the marketing page, to see what you actually get for $0. Blink came out on top for the free tier that's worth using.
body_markdown:
## What we looked for


A lot of "free AI website builder" lists just confirm a free tier exists, then stop. That answers the wrong question. Someone actually building a website needs to know whether the free tier can carry a real business site, not just whether the sign-up page has a $0 button.


- **Does it look like a real website, or a template with your name on it?** The whole promise of AI is that you describe a business and get something built around that business. A lot of tools generate into a fixed template instead, which is why so much AI-built output looks the same regardless of what you asked for.
- **Can you actually change things after it's built?** The first draft is never the last word. We checked whether editing means clicking an element and describing the change, or fighting a drag-and-drop canvas, or regenerating the whole page and losing what worked.
- **Does it handle SEO, or just tell you to figure it out?** A site nobody can find isn't finished. We checked whether the free tier includes real search and AI-visibility tooling, meta tags, sitemaps, structured data, or whether that's a paid add-on or a manual checklist.
- **Is it actually easy to use, not just marketed as easy?** Some of these tools genuinely take a plain-English description and go. Others still expect you to know what a template, a section, or a breakpoint is before you can finish anything.
- **No card required to start.** If a tool asks for billing details before you've seen anything, it isn't really free.
- **Real features, not a locked demo.** A free plan that hides the database, the AI edits, or the export behind a paywall is a trial with extra steps.
- **What it costs to actually go live.** Some free plans publish instantly by pushing ads onto your site that you can't remove without paying. Blink publishes live for free with zero ads, and only charges for a custom domain of your own. We say exactly which model each tool uses below.
- **Usage limits that don't quietly starve you.** Daily credits that reset beat a monthly cap that runs out on day 12.

Most of these prices are the beginning of the bill, not the end. Seat fees, credit top-ups, renewal jumps, and paywalled basics push the real cost higher almost everywhere on this list. Blink is the one flat, transparent number: $25/mo covers hosting, your own domain, and Blink Claw agents running in the background to help grow the site, with no upsell waiting on the next screen.


## The 9 free AI website builders, ranked


### 1. Blink


*Best overall free tier, live from day one*


Blink homepage


Blink


Blink's free plan is not a stripped-down demo of the real product, it is the real product, published live on a real Blink subdomain from the moment you're done. You get 5 build credits a day, capped at 30 a month, and every one of them runs the same AI agent, the same database, and the same authentication that paying customers use. Nothing about the build experience is watered down to push an upgrade.


- Full-stack, premium websites from the first prompt: a real SQL database, six sign-in providers, file storage, all on the free tier.
- Publishes live immediately on a Blink subdomain, with zero ads bolted onto your site.
- No credit card required to start building.
- Visual Editing and the SEO/AEO scanner both work on the free tier, not just on paid plans.


**Free plan:** 5 credits/day, capped 30/mo, live on a Blink subdomain, no ads, no card required. Starter at $25/mo is one flat, transparent price: your own domain, production hosting, and Blink Claw agents working 24/7 in the background to help grow the site. No add-ons waiting on the next screen.[Start free at blink.new →](https://blink.new/)


### 2. Wix


Wix will put a live URL in front of visitors for free, like Blink does, and the difference is what's riding along with it. Wix pushes its own ads onto your site to pay for that free hosting, ads you did not choose and cannot remove without upgrading.


- Publishes live immediately on a Wix subdomain, free plan included.
- The free site carries ads Wix pushes onto your page, ads that ruin the experience for anyone visiting it, and you cannot remove them without paying.
- Once you've picked a template you can't switch it later, and there's no way to export the site at all.
- SEO is a checklist you work through by hand, not something the tool scans and fixes for you.


**Heads up:** Free today means ads bolted onto your site that you never agreed to and cannot remove without paying. Wix's own help center also states the site must stay hosted on Wix's servers, permanently.


**Free plan:** Live publishing with Wix ads pushed onto your site and a Wix subdomain. Light plan $17/mo removes the ads and adds a custom domain, then bookings, ecommerce, and most real business tools sit behind higher tiers still.


### 3. Framer


Framer homepage


Blink


Framer's free plan is generous for a design-first tool, 500 credits and a live subdomain, and it's aimed at people who already think in terms of a canvas rather than a prompt.


- 500 free credits, publishes live on a Framer subdomain.
- Credits reset on the 1st of the month with no rollover, so a slow month wastes what you didn't use and a busy one runs out fast.
- Robots.txt editing and redirects are locked to the Pro plan, so real SEO control isn't part of the free tier.
- Getting the most out of it means learning a design canvas, not describing what you want.


**Heads up:** The free tier's SEO ceiling is low, and leads captured through a Framer site have nowhere to land except an inbox or a webhook.


**Free plan:** 500 credits, Framer subdomain, 1GB bandwidth. Basic $10/mo adds a custom domain.


### 4. Lovable


Lovable homepage


Blink


Lovable's free plan is aimed at prototyping a working app rather than a marketing site, and it's one of the few here that both publishes live for free and includes a genuinely useful SEO feature at no cost.


- Free SEO and AEO review with one-click fixes, on every plan including free.
- Stopped build requests still spend credits, so a debugging session that goes nowhere still costs you.
- A custom domain is paid-plans-only, and there's no native path from a captured lead into a CRM.
- It's built for prototyping a functional app, not designing a business website that has to convert.


**Heads up:** This is a prototyping tool wearing a website builder's clothes. Fine for testing an idea, not built for a business site.


**Free plan:** 5 credits/day, capped 30/mo, subdomain + badge. Pro from $25/mo for a custom domain.


### 5. Base44


Base44 homepage


Blink


Base44's free plan is generous on paper, up to 5 apps with real authentication and database functionality, no card required.


- Free plan supports up to 5 apps with real auth and a database, no card required.
- Output leans on Base44's own template gallery, labeled "customize template," not a design generated from your brief.
- No live publishing without a paid plan, and nothing built around conversion or motion at all.
- Owned by Wix, and the design system feels just as boxed in.


**Heads up:** What you get is functional, not persuasive. There's no path from a free build to a live site without paying.


**Free plan:** Up to 5 apps, real auth and database, no card required. Starter $16/mo for a custom domain.


### 6. Durable


Durable homepage


Blink


Durable will hand you a generated layout in about 30 seconds, which makes it the fastest thing on this list to try, even if what you get is thin.


- Fastest generation time of anything tested, a live draft in about 30 seconds.
- The layout looks the same across industries because structure locks the moment it generates.
- A branded live URL needs the paid Launch plan, roughly $22 to $25/mo.
- No serious motion story at all, and the thinnest feature set of anything on this list outside its built-in CRM.


**Heads up:** Fast to try, thin to actually use. The 30 seconds is the best part of the experience.


**Free plan:** Durable subdomain, trial only. Launch plan roughly $22 to $25/mo for a branded URL.


### 7. Replit


Replit homepage


Blink


Replit's pricing page doesn't show a permanent free plan for a published, hosted app, the way Blink and Base44 do. If your priority is genuinely free hosting, this isn't the pick.


- A real SEO Agent that scans, rates, and fixes issues with a click.
- No confirmed free tier for a real, hosted, published site on the current pricing page.
- No click-to-edit visual page, so anyone who can't read code is stuck describing cosmetic fixes one prompt at a time.
- Nothing about the output is trained on conversion or business design, it reads like an app, not a website.


**Heads up:** Built for developers, not business owners. If reading code isn't your thing, every small fix becomes a negotiation with the agent.


**Free plan:** Not confirmed for a published, hosted app. Core starts at $18/mo billed annually.


### 8. Squarespace


Squarespace homepage


Blink


Squarespace has the best-looking template catalogue in this entire comparison, and it makes you pay to find out, there's no permanent free plan, only a 14-day trial.


- Roughly 200 designer templates, the largest catalogue in this comparison.
- No free plan at all, only a 14-day trial that doesn't let you publish live.
- Cannot edit robots.txt or the sitemap on any plan, a hard ceiling if organic search matters.
- Still a template you're renting, not a design generated for your specific business.


**Heads up:** The best-looking templates in this comparison, and the least amount of SEO control on any plan.


**Free plan:** None. 14-day trial, no live publish. Basic $19/mo.


### 9. Hostinger


Hostinger website builder page


Blink


Hostinger doesn't have a free plan either, and its advertised price is the most misleading number in this comparison.


- A custom domain is bundled free for the first year on paid plans.
- No free plan at all, and the advertised ~$2.99/mo actually requires $143.52 paid upfront for 48 months.
- Unused AI credits expire, and undoing a change doesn't refund what it cost.
- Export is one-way and can't even be reused on Hostinger's own hosting without extra work.


**Heads up:** The sticker price is the best thing about it. Everything after signup is a renewal trap.


**Free plan:** None. 14-day trial. Premium ~$2.99/mo requires a 48-month prepay, and renews at $10.99/mo after, over 3x the advertised price.


## Frequently asked questions


Blink. Its free plan includes the full product, a real database, real authentication, and the same AI agent paid users get, published live on a Blink subdomain with no ads and no card required. The only thing that costs money is a custom domain of your own, which starts at $25/mo. Most other free plans that publish live hand you ads, like Wix does, or a thinner product missing the features that made you want AI in the first place.


Yes, with several tools on this list, including Blink, Wix, Framer, Lovable, and Base44. None of them ask for billing details to start. Squarespace and Hostinger are the exceptions here, both require a trial signup and neither publishes live for free.


Usually one of three things: the output carries ads and the vendor's subdomain, the real features (database, export, SEO tools) are locked behind a paid plan, or the free tier technically exists but expires into a trial. Blink's free tier avoids the first two by including the full product for free and being upfront that publishing live is the one paid step.


Blink, Wix, Framer, and Lovable all put a live URL in front of visitors on their free plans. The difference is what comes with it: Blink publishes on a Blink subdomain with zero ads, while Wix pushes its own ads onto your site to cover the cost of hosting it for free. Base44 and Durable require a paid plan before anything goes live at all.
